note: Maps each World Bank region to the code of its OFFICIAL regional aggregate,
so the dashboard can use the Bank's own published subtotal as the regional
benchmark rather than computing one from the countries on screen.
These are the seven 'all income levels' aggregates. Do NOT substitute the
'excluding high income' variants (EAP, ECA, LAC, MNA, SSA) — those cover a
different set of economies and would not match the country rows above them.
`names` exists because the two data paths disagree about region labels.
The REST API returns some names with trailing whitespace, and the World Bank
reclassified the Middle East region to include Afghanistan and Pakistan: the
January 2026 bulk CSV already carries the new name on the AGGREGATE row while
its COUNTRY rows still carry the old one. Matching on a list of accepted
names, compared with whitespace collapsed, absorbs both discrepancies.
Add a name here rather than teaching either script about a specific region.
`world` is the same idea one level up. A country's sparkline is drawn
against its region's aggregate; a region's sparkline needs something to be
drawn against in turn, and the World aggregate is the only honest choice
from the same source. It is kept separate from `aggregates` because the
world is not a region and must never appear as a row.

names: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan
